commits.message:
bf16 nets: pad batches to fixed sizes (gen7_net.bucket) so oneDNN stops building kernels for every new size

With BRIDGE_NET_BF16=1 the rollouts' changing batch sizes made oneDNN build a kernel
for each new shape and grow its cache. Padding each bf16 call (Bf16Forward and the
FitScorer's bf16 layers) to about 25 fixed sizes and cutting the padding off: in the
sandbox (Sapphire Rapids) self-play goes from 26.0 to 13.9 CPU-s a board and a worker's
peak memory from 2.3 to 1.4 GB, the same cards on 6 boards, outputs bit-identical.
Not yet measured on the Zen 4 boxes. BRIDGE_NET_BUCKETS=0 turns it off.

mailbridge: a mailbox for a Claude session, relayed by a box through an encrypted channel branch

mailbridge.py runs on the box (IMAP poll and SMTP send each minute, allow-listed
recipients); client.py runs in the session; branch mail/coord carries CMS
sign-then-encrypt blobs because the repository is public. Tested end to end with
tests/test_mailbridge.py against a local bare repository and a fake transport;
the Gmail transport is untested until the live box.
